requirements.title: Component initialization selects a constant value, a null initializer or an initial data target
requirements.source: 7.5.4.6, R743, R743.constant-expression-alternative, R743.null-initialization-alternative, R743.initial-data-target-alternative; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 96-98.
requirements.definition: A component-initialization is an equals sign followed by a constant expression, or an arrow followed by null-init or initial-data-target. These alternatives do not grant ordinary expression or pointer-assignment syntax indiscriminately: the component attributes and descendants retain their separate restrictions. A procedure component uses proc-decl and its own procedure-pointer initializer.

requirements.oracle: Compile admission and minimal syntax repairs are separate from the p3-p6 runtime effects. Use only exact small integer values and independently justified shape/target premises.
requirements.oracle_limitation: C813 requires NULL() with no arguments for null-init; general NULL(MOLD=...) permissions do not extend that use. An arbitrary function call is not thereby a constant expression or an initial data target. Do not claim conversion, allocation or association effects from parser acceptance. Every planned negative needs a source-minimal conforming repair and a subject-specific primary diagnostic at its actual point or independently justified bounded relation. Required reporting need not be fatal. Unsupported facilities, unrelated recovery, crashes, verifier/resource failures and timeouts do not establish the intended condition. requirements.title: An initial data target is a designator
requirements.definition: The initial-data-target syntax is a designator, not an arbitrary data expression or procedure invocation. C770 further limits the object and designator selectors; C769 separately tests compatibility with the actual component.

requirements.title: Component initialization requires the double-colon separator
requirements.definition: When a data component declaration contains component-initialization, a double-colon separator must precede its component-decl-list. The condition concerns the list separator, not an array bound, substring colon or procedure-component declaration.
requirements.oracle: The missing-separator contrast changes one declaration token sequence and preserves a complete valid type body. It is not an EOF or name-lookup test.

requirements.title: Initialized components have only constant or deferred type parameters and bounds
requirements.source: 7.5.4.6, C767, C767.initialization-present, C767.every-type-parameter, C767.every-array-bound, C767.colon-or-constant-expression; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 96-98.
requirements.definition: If component-initialization is present, every type parameter and every array bound of that component must be a colon or a constant expression. Both the condition and the universal every-parameter/every-bound qualification matter. A valid specification expression is not necessarily a constant expression.

requirements.oracle: Use legal parameter declarations in R726 order and separate KIND constant primaries from LEN specification primaries. Repairs preserve the same uninitialized component rather than changing its dynamic specification into a different test.
requirements.oracle_limitation: All independent component declaration restrictions remain in force. Colon is not permission to initialize an ALLOCATABLE component with = or =>. requirements.title: Initializer punctuation restricts the component attributes
requirements.source: 7.5.4.6, C768, C768.arrow-needs-pointer, C768.equals-excludes-pointer, C768.equals-excludes-allocatable; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 96-98.
requirements.definition: An arrow in component-initialization requires POINTER in the component attributes. An equals initializer permits neither POINTER nor ALLOCATABLE there. A data target and NULL() share the arrow attribute condition, while allocatable initial status does not come from an explicit component initializer.
requirements.oracle: Each attribute contrast has one forbidden attribute relationship; do not combine POINTER and ALLOCATABLE into a separate mutually-exclusive-attribute error.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A report about an unsupported target facility or another type definition is not a report of the specified component attribute relationship. requirements.title: An initialized data pointer component is compatible with its target
requirements.source: 7.5.4.6, C769, C769.initial-data-target-condition, C769.named-component-compatibility; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 96-98.
requirements.definition: When an initial-data-target occurs in a component declaration, the named component must be data-pointer-initialization compatible with that target. Paragraph2 defines the complete conjunction of type compatibility, equal rank, equal nondeferred type parameters and the conditional contiguity requirement.

requirements.title: An initial data target has permanent object and constant-selector premises
requirements.source: 7.5.4.6, C770, C770.nonallocatable-variable, C770.noncoindexed-variable, C770.target-attribute, C770.save-attribute, C770.no-vector-subscript, C770.constant-subscripts, C770.constant-section-subscripts, C770.constant-substring-start, C770.constant-substring-end; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 96-98.
requirements.definition: An initial-data-target designator must designate a nonallocatable, noncoindexed variable with TARGET and SAVE and no vector subscript. Each subscript, section subscript and substring endpoint in the designator must be a constant expression. An initializer on a local variable can imply SAVE, so omission of the SAVE spelling alone does not establish the missing attribute.

requirements.title: Allocatable components begin with unallocated status
requirements.definition: Allocatable components are initialized to unallocated status. This is an initialization property, not a claim that an allocated component remains unallocated after subsequent allocation, construction or assignment. It does not require a component-initialization specifier and must be distinguished from the p8 definition of a type with default initialization.

pending.allocation-event-use-graph: Pending the exact canonical initial-status, INTENT(OUT), constructor, SOURCE= and assignment relationships; copied/assigned allocation status is not this initial-state witness.

requirements.oracle: Only allocation-status inquiries are permitted before explicit component allocation. A later allocation and defined payload can provide a separate guard/control.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Do not infer a component value, shape or dynamic type from unallocated status. Automatic unallocation is not an invented explicit =NULL() component initializer.
requirements.dependencies: 7.5.4.6 p1/p8;9.7 and allocation-status rules;7.5.10 p3/p6-p8, PDF107-108;19.5/19.6.

requirements.title: Data-pointer-initialization compatibility is a qualified conjunction
requirements.source: 7.5.4.6, p2, p2.compatibility-term, p2.type-compatible, p2.same-rank, p2.nondeferred-parameter-values, p2.contiguous-pointer-condition, p2.contiguous-target; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 96-98.
requirements.definition: The named compatibility relation holds when the pointer is type compatible with the target, ranks agree, every nondeferred pointer parameter agrees with the corresponding target parameter, and a CONTIGUOUS pointer has a contiguous target. The definition applies to a pointer variable or component; it is not general intrinsic assignment compatibility and does not perform a value conversion.

requirements.title: Pointer component default disassociation
requirements.source: 7.5.4.6, p3, p3.null-initializer-condition, p3.initial-disassociation, p3.later-disassociation-events; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 96-98.
requirements.definition: When null-init on a pointer component is specified, the component is initially disassociated, or becomes disassociated at the events specified by 19.5.2.4(5). The event alternatives retain their nonpointer/nonallocatable/unsaved and no-SOURCE conditions; they are not an instruction to reset association after every assignment or reference.

requirements.oracle: Use ASSOCIATED only after the declared initializer or exact default-initialization event establishes defined association status. Non-null targets outlive every use; target values and called procedures have separately established semantics.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Never query a dangling or never-initialized pointer. A TARGET attribute does not imply a defined data value. Procedure-component PASS/NOPASS, target class and interface compatibility retain their canonical restrictions. A type-only admission is not a runtime association effect.

requirements.definition: When initial-data-target on a data pointer component is specified, the component is initially associated with that target, or becomes associated with that target at the events specified by 19.5.2.3(5). requirements.title: Value defaults establish the expression value with intrinsic-assignment conversion
requirements.source: 7.5.4.6, p6.constant-expression-condition, p6.initial-and-event-definition, p6.value-from-expression, p6.conversion-if-necessary, p6.type-agreement, p6.parameter-agreement, p6.shape-agreement; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 96-98.
requirements.definition: A nonpointer component with a constant-expression initializer is initially defined or becomes defined at the canonical definition events. Its value is obtained from that expression and, when needed, converted under intrinsic assignment to agree with the component type, type parameters and shape. C768 independently excludes ALLOCATABLE from this explicit value-initializer form.

pending.definition-event-use-graph: Pending canonical links to19.6.3(3) and19.6.5(19),(23),(24),(28), with SOURCE= and explicit initialization kept distinct.

requirements.oracle: Use exact small integers and default-character equality. Do not infer arbitrary real rounding, physical representation or conversion correctness from repeated literal comparisons. Read only initialized/otherwise defined subcomponents.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Partial defaults do not define every sibling. Array scalar expansion and actual array-expression conformance are distinct. The default value is not necessarily reapplied during intrinsic assignment or SOURCE= allocation.

requirements.title: An enclosing component value default overrides nested defaults
requirements.definition: When an initialized component has a derived type with its own component defaults, the outer constant-expression initialization overrides the nested defaults. The semantics are as though only the overriding initialization were specified, not a later reapplication of the inner defaults over the supplied value.

pending.override-event-use-graph: Pending the exact interaction with default-initialized subcomponent classification and constructor defaults; no double initialization or finalizer side effect is invented.

requirements.oracle: Construct valid constant derived values with complete required components. Choose simple nonfinalizable types so no unreviewed finalization count enters the oracle.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The clause is not permission to use an invalid constant constructor or inaccessible component. Pointer initial target/lifetime restrictions remain necessary.

requirements.title: Explicit type-declaration initialization overrides component defaults
requirements.definition: Explicit initialization of an object in a type declaration statement overrides its default initialization. This precedence concerns an explicit initializer, not an ordinary executable assignment or a claim that default initialization implicitly supplies SAVE.

pending.explicit-initialization-use-graph: Pending canonical8.2/C7104/C7107/constant-expression and SAVE relationships; constructor omission/default behavior retains7.5.10 ownership.

requirements.oracle: Compare separate explicitly initialized and only-default-initialized objects. All referenced constant components are defined and accessible.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No claim is made that an arbitrary executable expression is a legal declaration initializer. Explicit initialization may imply SAVE under its own rule.

requirements.title: Default initialization does not itself imply SAVE
requirements.definition: Default initialization alone does not give an object the SAVE attribute. An object can separately be saved by explicit declaration, containing scope or other canonical rules. Initialization on entry and retention of prior association, allocation or value state must not be conflated.

pending.save-source-use-graph: Pending canonical module/main/submodule implicit SAVE and declaration-initialization relationships; do not use such a scope as evidence of automatic local storage.

requirements.oracle: Observe state only while defined in each invocation. Use counters or distinct arguments outside the tested local variable to distinguish invocations.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No storage address, stack layout or attempted read after lifetime termination is part of the oracle. The rule does not prohibit an independent SAVE attribute.

requirements.title: Default-initialized subcomponents exclude enclosing initialized subobjects
requirements.definition: A subcomponent is default-initialized when its containing object type specifies default initialization for that component and the subcomponent is not a subobject of an object that is itself default-initialized or explicitly initialized. These containing-object exclusions prevent nested defaults from independently overriding an enclosing supplied initialization.

pending.default-initialized-container-exclusion: Pending canonical linkage to the p6 outer-default override witness, not an additional duplicate execution.
pending.explicitly-initialized-container-exclusi: Pending canonical linkage to the p6 explicit object override witness.
pending.subobject-and-event-use-graph: Pending the exact9.4.2 subobject relation and19.5/19.6 event users; a pointer target is not treated as the same subobject as the pointer.

requirements.oracle: Use complete nesting and source-use relations, not an implementation model that initializes every reachable memory location.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A dereferenced pointer target is not a subobject of its pointer-containing base object merely because the pointer component is a subobject for status purposes.

requirements.title: Type and object default-initialization classification use direct components
requirements.source: 7.5.4.6, p8, p8.type-direct-component-condition, p8.object-type-condition; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 96-98.
requirements.definition: A type has default initialization if component-initialization is specified for any direct component of the type. An object has default initialization when its type has it. Under3.30.1, direct components include components reached recursively through nonpointer nonallocatable components; the term is not limited to the outermost declaration list and does not traverse pointer targets or allocatable component objects. A pointer component can still have its own initializer. This classification is separate from the initially unallocated status of allocatable components.

pending.direct-component-classification: Pending a finite source/use relation for types with and without an actual direct component-initialization; preserve the canonical direct-component definition.
pending.object-type-classification: Pending canonical consumers linking the object classification to its type, not a runtime bit or an invented inquiry intrinsic.
pending.nested-direct-component-classification: Pending the3.30.1 recursive path through ordinary nonpointer nonallocatable components to a nested component initializer.
pending.pointer-and-allocatable-recursion-bounda: Pending the direct-component traversal boundary: a pointer component own initializer counts, but traversal into its target or an allocatable component object does not follow3.30.1.
pending.inherited-and-recursive-use-graph: Pending an independently reviewed graph through direct versus potential subobject components, inheritance and p7; do not infer all recursive cases from one type.

requirements.oracle: This is a source-level classification with explicitly pending consumer evidence, not a parser-only proof or a new language inquiry.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The p1 allocation-status property does not automatically imply that the p8 syntactic condition was met. Complete direct/inherited/recursive use accounting needs its own reviewed graph.
